title: Grokked Transformers are Implicit Reasoners: A Mechanistic Journey to the Edge of Generalization
abstract: This paper explores whether transformers can learn to reason implicitly over parametric knowledge. Through a mechanistic study, we find that transformers can learn implicit reasoning, but only through grokking, i.e., extended training far beyond overfitting.

sections.title: The Core Insight
sections.content:
Imagine you're trying to solve a puzzle. You have all the pieces, but you need to figure out how they fit together. This is similar to how transformers work when they're trying to reason implicitly. They have all the information they need, but they need to learn how to use it. We found that transformers can learn to reason implicitly, but only if they're trained for a long time, a phenomenon known as grokking.

So, why does grokking happen? It's because the transformer is trying to find the most efficient way to solve the problem. It's like finding the shortest path to the solution.

sections.title: How It Works
sections.content:
We studied how transformers learn to reason implicitly by creating a synthetic dataset and training a transformer from scratch. We found that the transformer can learn to perform implicit reasoning, but only through grokking. The speed of improvement in generalization correlates with the ratio between inferred and atomic facts in training.

We also found that the transformer exhibits different levels of systematicity across reasoning types. For composition, the transformer fails to systematically generalize, but for comparison, it succeeds.

sections.title: Benchmark Results
sections.content:
We compared the performance of our grokked transformer with state-of-the-art language models like GPT-4-Turbo and Gemini-1.5-Pro. We found that our grokked transformer achieves near-perfect accuracy on a challenging reasoning task, while the other models fail badly.

These results demonstrate the power of parametric memory for complex reasoning and highlight the importance of grokking in achieving systematic generalization.

sections.title: Why This Matters
sections.content:
Our findings have significant implications for the development of language models that can reason implicitly. They suggest that grokking is a crucial factor in achieving systematic generalization and that the transformer architecture needs to be modified to improve its generalization capabilities.

We also found that the configuration of the generalizing circuit is important for achieving systematic generalization. This has implications for the design of more efficient and effective language models.

sections.title: Key Innovations
sections.content:
Our study introduces several key innovations, including the use of a synthetic dataset to study implicit reasoning and the development of a mechanistic approach to analyze the internal workings of the transformer.

We also found that the transformer exhibits different levels of systematicity across reasoning types, which has implications for the design of more efficient and effective language models.

sections.title: Try It Yourself
sections.content:
We provide a GitHub repository with our code and data, allowing you to try out our approach and experiment with different settings.

You can use our code to train your own grokked transformer and evaluate its performance on various reasoning tasks.
